title: Reconcile customer monthly usage delta after autoscaling evictions
creator: Aisha Patel
description: During a customer-reported billing reconciliation for February end-of-month, we observed consistent negative deltas and unexplained monthly usage drops for several Dedicated tenants that experienced autoscaler-driven pod evictions. Affected customers reported undercharges (they actually used more tokens than the invoice reflected) and inconsistent ledger lines between the realtime usage stream and the monthly aggregate. The issue correlates with high-churn workloads and autoscaling events in the dedicated fleet. This ticket tracks triage, root cause, remediation, and customer reconciliation steps.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Deploy dedicated workload simulator with sustained short-lived sessions that exercise streaming generation and KV cache writes
2) Configure cluster autoscaler to aggressively scale down (simulate binpacking / resource pressure)
3) Trigger scripted evictions of serving pods (kubectl drain with --force) during mid-stream responses
4) Observe token-delta stream in metrics pipeline and compare with ledger ingest output (token_aggregator) to detect mismatches
root_cause_summary: The metering agent running on serving pods buffers per-session token deltas in an in-memory windowed journal and periodically checkpoints to the central ledger service. When pods are evicted abruptly (SIGKILL due to eviction grace < preStop flush), the in-memory buffer is not durably committed. Simultaneously, client-side retry logic resubmits partially-completed requests which generate new token deltas. The combination of lost checkpoint commits and replayed requests leads to undercounting in some flows and double-counting in others depending on ordering and race conditions. Additionally, the aggregator assumed monotonic session sequence numbers from the pod which were reset after restart, causing replays to be accepted instead of deduplicated.
mitigation_deployed: Temporarily increased pod terminationGracePeriod to 90s for affected dedicated clusters to allow flush of buffered deltas
Pinned autoscaler scale-down threshold to 20% fewer evictions for Dedicated tier until durable journal patch lands
Issued customer-facing interim memo explaining expected reconciliation and that invoices will be adjusted proactively for impacted tenants
proposed_fix: Make pod-side metering agent durable: write token-delta journal to local persistent volume in append-only batches and switch aggregator to accept only strictly-monotonic session sequence numbers with idempotency keys. Add preStop hook that blocks termination until journal is flushed and acknowledged by ledger service. Add server-side deduplication using request-level idempotency keys for streaming endpoints. Add unit and e2e tests to exercise eviction scenarios and retries.
acceptance_criteria: 1) No token-delta loss observed when simulating forced evictions with terminationGracePeriod=0 in staging (deterministic harness)
2) Aggregator rejects duplicate session sequence numbers after restart in all tested cases
3) Monthly reconciliation job reports <0.1% delta across synthetic tenants under eviction-heavy workloads
4) Customers with previously reported deltas have reconciled ledger entries and manual invoice adjustments applied where required
